about.title: Claremont Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Claremont's tree-lined streets and college-town pace don't stop crashes from happening, especially where Indian Hill Boulevard, Baseline Road, and Foothill Boulevard funnel traffic on and off SR-210. Public records show 192 injury collisions here in the most recent year, with 272 people hurt and 7 lives lost. Fridays between 5 and 7 p.m. see more reported crashes than any other window, likely tied to end-of-week commuting and weekend travel. Whatever the cause of your collision, the days right after matter: insurance adjusters move fast, and evidence like skid marks, dashcam footage, and witness memories fade quickly. LawProactive doesn't practice law or charge fees; we simply connect injured Claremont residents with an independent personal injury attorney who can evaluate the crash, handle insurer communication, and pursue compensation on a contingency basis, meaning no fee unless you recover.

whyChoose.title: Why Act Quickly After a Claremont Crash

items.title: California's Clock Is Ticking
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash date to file a personal injury claim in California, but if a government vehicle or roadway defect was involved, that window can shrink to as little as six months. Waiting too long can close the door on compensation entirely.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Work in Your Favor
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, so even if you're partly blamed for a collision on a busy corridor like SR-210, you can still recover damages reduced by your share of fault. An attorney can help make sure your percentage of blame isn't overstated by the insurer.

items.title: Avoid Giving a Recorded Statement Too Soon
items.desc: The other driver's insurer may ask for a recorded statement quickly, hoping you'll say something that limits their payout. You're not obligated to provide one, and an independent attorney can speak for you while evidence from the scene is preserved.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after a car accident in Claremont?
items.answer: California generally allows two years from the date of the crash to file a personal injury lawsuit. If your accident involved a government-owned vehicle or a road maintained by a public entity, the deadline to file a claim can be as short as six months. It's best to start the process early so evidence and deadlines don't work against you.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the accident?
items.answer: California follows a pure comparative fault rule, meaning you can still recover compensation even if you share some responsibility for the crash. Your total award is simply reduced by your percentage of fault. This matters at busy Claremont intersections like Indian Hill and Baseline where fault can be contested.

items.question: Should I talk to the other driver's insurance company?
items.answer: You're not required to give a recorded statement to the other party's insurer, and doing so early can sometimes hurt your claim. It's generally safer to let an independent attorney communicate on your behalf while details from the accident, such as those involving Foothill Boulevard traffic, are still fresh and documented.
